subject: KiteBridge integration: request for SLA routing & latency escalation
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@kitebridge.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent latency spikes on KiteBridge prod -> Redwood inference (region us-west)

Hi Ben —

We're seeing intermittent latency spikes and occasional token-level timeouts when routing calls to the Redwood hosted endpoint for our v2 connector. Impact: user-facing errors for a small subset (~2%) of requests, but spikes correlate with peak batch windows and are crossing the 200ms P95 target.

Quick summary:
- First observed: 2027-04-09 22:00 UTC, recurring during US morning traffic
- Error pattern: delays at request routing stage, not obvious 500s from model itself
- Logs attached: kitebridge_error_logs_0409.zip (sample traces + request IDs)

We need: a short-term routing/fallback to a compatible model variant and a longer-term runbook for partner escalations and SLA routing. Can you confirm who on Redwood ops/partner eng will own triage? KiteBridge legal/product teams expect an ops update within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Priya
Partner Ops — KiteBridge
priya@kitebridge.io

attachments: kitebridge_error_logs_0409.zip (zip, 6.3 MB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Priya Shah <priya@kitebridge.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes on KiteBridge prod -> Redwood inference (region us-west)

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I've pulled this into a short action plan below and looped in our integrations lead and partner engineer.

Immediate (within 4h):
- Routing fallback: We'll enable automatic fallback to model-variant rb-medium-qa in us-west for requests that hit our 150ms routing queue threshold. This should reduce tail latency while preserving output quality.
- Temporary rate smoothing: apply 5% burst smoothing on your connector's API key to avoid sudden queue spikes.
- Contact: sergio_alvarez will own the triage and monitor real-time traces.

Follow-up (EOD + 48h):
- Runbook: marissa_cole will draft a concise partner SLA escalation runbook (canary + route failover + logs to collect).
- RCA data: Please send any more traces with request IDs; we'll correlate with JIRA INFR-11234.

I've created the Jira ticket and will add notes from the logs you sent. Sergio — can you confirm we have a safe fallback to rb-medium-qa for KiteBridge and a plan to roll back if it changes quality for them? Marissa — can you own the runbook draft and share a link?

Ben
Ben Carter

Questions from our side:
- Will fallback to rb-medium-qa be transparent to us or require schema changes?
- Can Redwood set an explicit SLA exception window so we can update affected customers?

We've also received a procurement escalation from KiteBridge Legal asking for documented mitigation steps and anticipated ETA. Priya will follow up with the formal request.

Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes on KiteBridge prod -> Redwood inference (region us-west)

Priya / team — status update and escalation path below. I'm also escalating to Ava given potential SLA communication to KiteBridge customers.

What we did (completed):
- Enabled automatic routing fallback to rb-medium-qa for any request that hits a routing queue >150ms. This is live in us-west as of 2027-04-11T14:10:00-07:00.
- Applied burst smoothing to the affected API key; smoothing metrics show a reduction in instantaneous queue depth.
- Collected correlated traces; attached is our initial runbook doc (RBODoc-runbook-v1.md) with instructions for on-call, fallback verification steps, and roll-back criteria.

Owners & next steps:
- Sergio Alvarez (Partner Ops) — owns live monitoring and will post hourly updates to JIRA INFR-11234 until stabilized.
- Marissa Cole (Partner Eng) — drafting a consolidated partner-facing SLA exception note and the permanent runbook. Expect draft by EOD Monday.
- Ava Chen (Head of Partnerships) — owning stakeholder comms and any credit/compensation conversations.

Temporary SLA exception: Redwood can provide a short exception window for incidents resulting from routing anomalies. Ava / legal will confirm language; Priya, please share the procurement/legal contact and we will route the formal exception.

If anything regresses, please flag immediately with request IDs and we will escalate to infra on-call. We'll keep hourly updates on JIRA:INFR-11234 and share a concise post-incident RCA within 72 hours.

Ben
